work_packages.name: A change that alters a registered exact image, on the Mac or in Chrome, is refused before it reaches main

items.statement: From a clean checkout, one command verifies every registered exact baseline at the current commit: it builds the release game and the Wasm page, cooks the valley, runs APPLE-TILE's native matrices and the four Chrome fixed captures, exits non-zero on any difference, refuses a dirty tree, and on a full pass writes a proof that names the content key.
items.ask: Does the verifier take every input from the checkout and its own fresh outputs, reading nothing from another task's scratch such as tmp/g3t-m0? Does its record hold the revision, the content key, the native binary's hash, the Wasm artefact hashes and the cooked root? Do its registry and the table in ARCHITECTURE.md list the same baselines, owners and covered paths?

items.statement: The Chrome comparison covers all 481 records of each of the four retained sets (day and night, submitted SDR and scene-linear): the identity fields are equal, and each fresh frame's decoded bytes hash to the retained digest. Every retained reference file is unchanged, and the owner's byte comparison behaves as before.
items.ask: Read the comparison and one verifier record. Is each fresh frame's hash computed again from its bytes, not copied from the candidate's manifest? Are all four sets and all 481 records of each compared? Did this work package's diff leave every file under the registered baselines byte-identical?

items.statement: `./dev check` passes a commit with no covered-path change beyond main without a proof, and refuses one with such a change unless a proof names its content key. A proof stops counting when a rebase brings in a covered-path change, and still counts when the rebase brings in only other paths.
items.ask: Read the test and the gate. Does the test drive fetch, rebase, gate and push against a throwaway remote, and show that remote's main unmoved after each refusal? Does `./dev check` run the gate, with no flag or environment variable that skips it?

items.statement: The loop's own `land`, run in a scratch clone against a local bare remote, refuses three regressions and leaves that remote's main unmoved: jitter on the game's default views, a night-only change and a Chrome-only change. Each fails the verifier by name, so no proof is written. A proved change rebased onto a covered-path commit is refused the same way.
items.ask: Do the retained patches, base revision, commands and logs let you reproduce each refusal? Does each verifier failure name the baseline, its owner and the comparison, and tell a changed image from a reference file that cannot be read? Was the real remote never pushed to?

items.statement: The time one verifier run and one gate check take is recorded from three runs each, with the load.
items.ask: What do the recorded runs show a covered-path landing pays, and how close is one verifier run to the loop's one-hour limit on a check?

work_packages.quality_bar: A merge gate in the manner of Rust's bors and a merge queue: the commit that reaches main is the commit that was tested, the comparison is exact and named, and it fails on the smallest real change.

work_packages.name: A commit that changes a registered reference image or its comparison is refused at the merge unless it records the refresh
work_packages.quality_bar: A lockfile's checksum, as in Cargo.lock or go.sum: a pinned file changes only in a commit that also changes its recorded digest, and the failure names the file, its owner and the rule.

items.statement: The registry lists each registered baseline's comparison files as the design's table names them, the verifier and `scripts/compare_v1_pixels.py` among them. For each baseline it holds a pin over the baseline's definition and the path and Git object ID of every protected file, and the refresh that last set the pin: the ruling's anchor in the module list, the module and the work package. One command computes every pin at the current commit, passes when each equals the registry's, and prints them.
items.ask: Read the guard and the registry. Is each pin computed from the commit's tree, over every field of the entry but the pin and the refresh, every tracked file of the reference and every comparison file? Does each baseline list every comparison file the design's table names for it? Does the first refresh of each baseline name an anchor that the module list holds?

items.statement: The guard refuses a change to a protected file, naming the baseline, its owner and each file that differs from the merge base with main: a changed byte in a reference file, a reference file added or removed, and a changed comparison file, with `scripts/compare_v1_pixels.py` and the verifier each tried. It refuses a protected file with an uncommitted change, a pin that changed while its refresh did not, and a refresh whose anchor the module list does not hold. It passes a commit that changes a reference together with its pin and a refresh naming an anchor the module list holds.
items.ask: Read the tests. Is each case decided by the function `./dev check` calls, in a Git repository made for the test, with the refusal's text asserted to name the baseline, the owner and the file? Is there a flag, an environment variable or a file other than the registry that makes the guard pass?

items.statement: `./dev check` runs the guard where it ran the gate, with no GPU, browser or build. The gate, the proof file and `proof_path` are gone: nothing under `scripts/` or `tools/` reads or writes a proof, and `verify --full` still writes its record with the content key.
items.ask: Does `./dev check` call the guard, and does it fail when the guard fails? Does a `verify --full` record still hold the revision, the content key, the binary and Wasm hashes and the cooked root?

items.statement: The verifier's scratch stays bounded. At its start, `verify --full` keeps the records of its latest runs and the captures of its latest failed run under `tmp/baseline-guard/`, and removes older ones. The numbers kept come from the measured size of a failed run, recorded with the free space the checkout of the run on main needs.
items.ask: Read the pruning and its tests. Can it remove anything outside `tmp/baseline-guard/` of its own checkout, the run in progress, or the latest failed run's captures? What do the recorded sizes say the checkout holds after a day of runs?

items.statement: Every registered exact baseline, on the Mac and in Chrome, passes on a main commit that contains the claimed one: this work package moved no retained image.
items.ask: Read this work package's diff. Is every file under the registered references unchanged, and does the registry still hold the same five baselines with their earlier fields as they were?

items.statement: `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `./dev help`, the engineering skill's building reference and the module list's exact-baseline rules describe the guard, the pins, and how a planned refresh, an edited comparison file and an added, redefined or retired baseline each record themselves. None still describes a proof file or a gate.
items.ask: Do the four documents agree with the guard as built? Does a builder making a planned refresh find in them every step it must take (regenerate, run `verify --full`, update the pin and the refresh, merge in one landing), and a planner retiring a baseline the record it must leave?

items.statement: The guard compares the registered set with the registry at the merge base with main. It refuses, naming the baseline and its owner: a baseline registered at the merge base that the commit neither registers nor retires, a changed field of a baseline's definition whose pin and refresh did not change with it, and a new baseline with no refresh. It passes a baseline moved to the retired list with a refresh naming an anchor the module list holds, and a redefined or added baseline whose pin and refresh are right.
items.ask: Read the tests. Does one remove a single baseline and leave every other entry, pin and refresh untouched, and is the refusal's text asserted to name that baseline? Is each case decided by the function `./dev check` calls, against the merge base's registry read from Git and not from the working tree?

work_packages.name: A passing exact-image record names the Wasm file that Chrome ran, and a run whose capture ran another fails
work_packages.quality_bar: A deployment pinned by digest, as `image@sha256:…` is: the record names the executable by a hash taken where it was loaded, and a run that loaded anything else fails by name.

items.statement: In a `verify --full` run the verifier builds one Wasm bundle, the proving bundle, records the SHA-256 of each of its files, and gives that folder to each of the four registered Chrome captures as its web root. For each capture it compares the SHA-256 the capture reports for the Wasm bytes its page instantiated with the recorded SHA-256 of `v1_game_bg.wasm`. When all four are equal the run can pass, and the record holds the reported hash against each baseline. When one differs, or one capture reports none, the run exits 1, names that baseline and its owner, and its record is not a pass.
items.ask: Read the verifier, the capture and the tests. Is the hash a capture reports taken inside the page from the bytes handed to WebAssembly, and not from the file on disk or the served file's hash? Does the verifier itself compare it, for every registered Chrome baseline, with the hash it recorded from the folder it gave that capture? Do the tests drive the verifier's real `verify` (stand-in child processes are fine) through the three cases: all equal, one different, one missing? Is any build or hash of the normal bundle left in the verifier, or any flag, environment variable or exit 75 by which a run with a different or missing hash is not a failure?

items.statement: One `verify --full` run on a clean checkout of this work package's candidate passes all five registered baselines, and its record is kept as `.orchestrate/evidence/BASELINE-GUARD/WP3/record.json`. In that record, for each of the four registered Chrome baselines, the Wasm SHA-256 the capture page instantiated equals the record's SHA-256 of `v1_game_bg.wasm`.
items.check: python3 -c 'import json; r=json.load(open(".orchestrate/evidence/BASELINE-GUARD/WP3/record.json")); ids=[b["id"] for b in json.load(open(".config/exact-baselines.json"))["baselines"] if "scene" in b]; w=r["wasm_artifact_hashes"]["v1_game_bg.wasm"]; assert r["passed"] is True and len(r["baselines"])==5 and len(ids)==4 and len(w)==64 and all(r["comparisons"][i]["instantiated_wasm_sha256"]==w for i in ids)'
items.ask: Read the record and the logs kept with it. Is its revision a commit of this work package, on a clean tree? Do its commands show one Wasm build, of the proving bundle, and that folder given to each of the four captures? Is each comparison's instantiated hash the one its capture wrote, and not copied from the verifier's own hash of the file?

items.statement: This work package changes nothing that is drawn or compared. Every retained reference file keeps its Git blob. Each of the five registry entries keeps its definition, and only its pin and its refresh change, the refresh naming `ruling-on-the-wasm-a-chrome-capture-runs`, `BASELINE-GUARD` and `WP3`. The comparison scripts other than the verifier are untouched. A capture that is not asked for the instantiated hash builds, serves, draws and writes what it did before.
items.ask: Read this work package's diff. Is every file under the registered references unchanged, and does the registry differ only in the five pins and refreshes? In `scripts/capture_v1_browser.mjs`, is reporting the instantiated hash the only change, and does a run that does not ask for it take the path it took before, with the same default bundle and the same manifest fields? In `scripts/test_capture_unjudged.py`, did only the stand-in for the verifier's web build change, with every assertion as it was? Are `examples/v1-game/web/build.sh`, `scripts/wasm_receipt.mjs`, the native matrices and the Chrome comparator untouched?
